349.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: Abū Dharr used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The roof of my house was opened while I was in Mecca. Then Jibrīl descended, opened my chest, washed it with Zamzam water, then brought a golden basin filled with wisdom and faith, poured it into my chest, and then closed it. Then he took me by the hand and ascended with me to the lowest heaven. When I came to the lowest heaven, Jibrīl said to the keeper of the heaven: Open! He said: Who is this? He said: This is Jibrīl. He said: Is anyone with you? He said: Yes, Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is with me. He said: Was he sent for? He said: Yes. When he opened, we went up above the lowest heaven, and there was a man sitting, with dark figures on his right and dark figures on his left. When he looked to his right he laughed, and when he looked to his left he wept. He said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous son! I said to Jibrīl: Who is this? He said: This is Ādam, and these figures on his right and left are the souls of his children. The people of the right among them are the people of Paradise, and the figures on his left are the people of the Fire. When he looks to his right he laughs, and when he looks to his left he weeps. – Then he ascended with me to the second heaven and said to its keeper: Open! Its keeper said to him the same as the first had said, and he opened. Anas said: He mentioned that he found in the heavens Ādam, Idrīs, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Ibrāhīm, may Allah’s blessings be upon them; it is not established how their stations were, except that he mentioned he found Ādam in the lowest heaven and Ibrāhīm in the sixth heaven. Anas said: When Jibrīl passed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by Idrīs, he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous brother! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Idrīs. Then I passed by Mūsā, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous brother! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Mūsā. Then I passed by ʿĪsā, and he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous prophet! I said: Who is this? He said: This is ʿĪsā. Then I passed by Ibrāhīm, and he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous son! I said: Who is this? He said: This is Ibrāhīm, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Shihāb said: Ibn Ḥazm informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥabba al-Anṣārī used to say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then I was taken up until I rose to a plain where I heard the scratching of the pens.” Ibn Ḥazm and Anas ibn Mālik said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then Allah made fifty prayers obligatory upon my community. I returned with that until I passed by Mūsā. He said: What has Allah made obligatory for your community? I said: He made fifty prayers obligatory. He said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that. So He turned to me again and removed half of it. I returned to Mūsā and said: He removed half of it. He said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear it. I returned, and He removed half of it. I returned to him, and he said: Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that. I returned to Him, and He said: They are five, and they are fifty; the word is not changed with Me. I returned to Mūsā, and he said: Return to your Lord. I said: I am ashamed before my Lord. Then he took me on until he brought me to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā); colors covered it, I do not know what they are. Then I was entered into Paradise, and in it were ḥabāyil of pearls, and its soil was musk.”
349.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The hadith stands at the beginning of the Book of Prayer, before the first chapter. Abū Dharr relates what the Prophet told of his journey through the heavens: the opening and washing of his chest, the ascent through the heavens with Jibrīl, and the meetings with Ādam, Idrīs, Mūsā, ʿĪsā and Ibrāhīm. Ibn Shihāb adds, through Ibn Ḥazm, statements from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥabba and, together with Anas, the imposition of fifty prayers that were reduced to five. The word ḥabāyil is left untranslated here.

350.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from ʿUrwa ibn az-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, she said: “Allah made the prayer obligatory when He made it obligatory as two rakʿas each, at home and on journey. The travel prayer was kept, and the prayer at home was increased.”
350.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This hadith also stands in the Book of Prayer, before the first chapter. ʿĀʾisha reports that the prayer was first made obligatory as two rakʿas each, at home and on journey; the travel prayer remained as it was, while the prayer at home was increased.
